### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 appears in about 26% of traces instead of about 58%, and its mean occurrences per trace drop from about 0.60 to 0.29; when it occurs, it appears later in the trace (mean position from about 0.18 to 0.43 of trace length). [OCC004, POS001]
- A02, A04 and A08 become more frequent: A02 rises from about 8% to 17% of traces, A04 from about 5% to 21%, and A08 from about 5% to 21%. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A10’s successors change: before, about 96% of A10 transitions go to A15; after, only about 35% go to A15, with A46, A44 and A16 each receiving about 10–12%. [DIR005]
- A14’s successors shift from mostly A10 (about 56%) and A15 (about 43%) to mostly A15 (about 77%) and only about 10% to A10. [DIR006]
- A25’s successors change from A32/A33 (about 54%/44%) to A26 (about 95%). [DIR008]
- A28’s successors change from A29 (about 97%) to A32/A33 (about 47% each). [DIR009]
- A32 and A33 both reduce their transitions to A26 and increase transitions to A29; A32 goes from about 43% to A26 to about 1%, and A33 from about 54% to A26 to about 1%. [DIR010, DIR011]
- The order between A26/A28 and A32/A33 reverses: before, A32/A33 preceded A26/A28 in nearly all traces; after, A26/A28 precede A32/A33 in about 96–98% of traces. [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- Lags confirm the reordering: A25–A26 moves from about 3 steps apart to 1 step; A25–A32 moves from 1–2 steps to 4–5 steps; A28–A29 moves from 1 step to 3 steps; A32–A29 moves from 4–5 steps to 1–2 steps. [LAG004, LAG006, LAG009, LAG012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reordering in the process: A10 is used less often and later, A14 now routes to A15 rather than through A10, and the segment involving A25, A26, A28, A29, A32 and A33 is rearranged so that A25 leads to A26/A28 instead of A32/A33, while A29 now follows A32/A33 instead of following A28. These conclusions rest on direct successor, relational and positional changes that are consistent across many activity pairs. The main limitation is that the windows are finite samples, so some frequency differences could reflect sampling variation, but the order reversals are based on nearly all traces and are unlikely to be chance artifacts. [OCC004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, LAG004, LAG006, LAG009, LAG012]
